hanbi_ch1.001: His hand is still held out. You haven't decided what to do about it yet when the ceiling clears its throat.
hanbi_ch1.003: I announced 04:57. It is 03:10. I apologise.
hanbi_ch1.004: Time spent inside a reconstruction is not charged to the night. I counted it anyway. I was built to be early.
hanbi_ch1.005: Please disregard the summons. You have one hour and forty-seven minutes.
hanbi_ch1.007: He looks at his hand as if it belongs to someone who was very sure of himself a minute ago.
hanbi_ch1.008: Take it, stand up, and sit straight back down. "False alarm."
hanbi_ch1.009: He gets pulled down with you. The sofa makes a noise like an accordion being apologised to.
hanbi_ch1.011: "Good. I wasn't ready to go yet."
hanbi_ch1.013: I'd only just started saying things. I'd like to keep going.
hanbi_ch1.014: Stay where you are. Let the extra hour arrive.
hanbi_ch1.015: He lowers his hand slowly and sits back down beside you. Neither of you mentions it. It was a good hand. It'll keep.
hanbi_ch1.017: What do you usually do with extra time?
hanbi_ch1.018: …I don't know. I've never had any. I give it to whoever's running late.
hanbi_ch1.019: He looks around the lounge for something that needs doing. His eyes stop at the low table by the window, where the dust sheet sits oddly over a flat shape.
hanbi_ch1.020: He lifts a corner the way you'd lift a blanket off a sleeping cat.
hanbi_ch1.021: A jigsaw. A thousand pieces, a harbour at dusk, almost finished. There's a gap in the sky the size of two open hands.
hanbi_ch1.022: The box lid is propped behind it. Taped to the lid, in marker gone brown with age: *DO NOT PUT AWAY. NEARLY DONE.*
hanbi_ch1.023: …It was here. That winter. I remember people doing two pieces on their way to the door.
hanbi_ch1.025: …Nobody put it away. They just covered it.
hanbi_ch1.026: …Someone should finish it. Before the morning. It shouldn't go in a skip with a hole in it.
hanbi_ch1.027: We have an hour and forty-seven minutes.
hanbi_ch1.029: The loose pieces are in the lid. Forty or so, and every one of them is sky.
hanbi_ch1.030: "How do you tell them apart? They're all the same blue."
hanbi_ch1.032: He lays three in a row on his palm. You look. They're the same blue.
hanbi_ch1.033: That one's tired. That one's got the sun behind it. That one's nearly a cloud.
hanbi_ch1.034: You look again. Annoyingly, he's right.
hanbi_ch1.035: "I'll take the tired blues. You take the smug ones."
hanbi_ch1.037: The ones near the sunset. They know what they've got.
hanbi_ch1.038: He sorts them into two piles without another word. He gives you the easier pile and thinks you haven't noticed.
hanbi_ch1.041: They always went back in the box when we moved. Four cities. Four boxes of nearly.
hanbi_ch1.042: …Then it's two people's first. That's better. Neither of us knows how it's supposed to feel.
hanbi_ch1.043: You work. It's slow and it's easy. The lamp hums. His sleeve brushes yours when he reaches for the top corner. The first time, he glances over to check. After that he leaves his chair where it is, and so do you.
hanbi_ch1.044: He talks more than you expected. It's all colours.
hanbi_ch1.045: Not that one. That's— grey-blue. Rain colour. It goes lower.
hanbi_ch1.046: …This is the last of the orange. Where the sun was.
hanbi_ch1.047: You realise what he's doing a few pieces later. He's saying them out loud. Nobody asked him to.
hanbi_ch1.049: …Practice. Tell me if you'd rather I stopped.
hanbi_ch1.051: The gap closes from the edges in. Two open hands. One. A fist. A thumbprint.
hanbi_ch1.052: Then the lid is empty, and there is one hole left in the sky.
hanbi_ch1.054: Tell me there's one in your sleeve.
hanbi_ch1.055: There isn't. There isn't one under the table or inside the box, either. You both check twice.
hanbi_ch1.056: You go down on your knees and feel under the orange sofa. You come up with a guitar pick, a hundred-won coin, and a great deal of dust.
hanbi_ch1.057: Guitar pick. From the man who was asleep on his case, probably.
hanbi_ch1.058: …Keep the coin. It's been waiting longest.
hanbi_ch1.059: You put the coin in your coat pocket. He looks at the hole in the sky the way he looks at a page.
hanbi_ch1.060: Then he opens his sketchbook at the back, where the cover is stiff grey card, and lays it against the puzzle.
hanbi_ch1.061: He traces the hole. Four quick curves. He scores the line with his thumbnail and works the shape out of the card with slow, patient folds.
hanbi_ch1.062: A jigsaw piece. Grey, and a little furry at the edges, and the right size.
hanbi_ch1.063: …What colour was it? The sky. There.
hanbi_ch1.065: …Neither have I. Somebody has to say.
hanbi_ch1.066: He's already holding the tin open. The yellow pencil is the shortest one in it, by now. Laundromat yellow.
hanbi_ch1.067: A lit window. Somebody left a light on, over the water.
hanbi_ch1.069: He's already holding the tin open. The green pencil is the shortest one in it, by now. Exit-sign green.
hanbi_ch1.070: Green. One of those strange skies you get right after the sun goes.
hanbi_ch1.072: He's already holding the tin open. The red pencil is the shortest one in it, by now. Vending-machine red.
hanbi_ch1.073: Red. The very last of the sunset. One dot of it.
hanbi_ch1.075: He's already holding the tin open. The blue pencil is the shortest one in it, by now. Archive Wall blue.
hanbi_ch1.076: Blue. A bit brighter than the rest. Like something's glowing behind it.
hanbi_ch1.078: He colours the card in small even strokes and holds it out to you, flat on his palm.
hanbi_ch1.080: Put two fingers on one edge of the piece. Wait for his. "Together."
hanbi_ch1.081: He looks at your fingers. Then he puts his own on the other edge, and you carry it over the harbour like something that could spill.
hanbi_ch1.082: It goes in with the small soft click that cardboard makes. Neither of you takes your hand away first.
hanbi_ch1.083: Try it upside down first. Frown. Turn it. Try again.
hanbi_ch1.085: I'm building suspense. Six years. It deserves a moment.
hanbi_ch1.086: It goes in. He tips his head to you, once, the way you'd acknowledge a good shot across a quiet room.
hanbi_ch1.087: "No. You. You never get to finish things."
hanbi_ch1.088: He holds the piece over the gap for a long time. His hand is steady. He isn't hesitating. He's taking his time over it.
hanbi_ch1.089: Then he presses it in with one finger, and lets out a breath like someone putting down shopping.
hanbi_ch1.090: A harbour at dusk. Finished. One piece of the sky is the wrong colour, and it's the only part you can look at.
hanbi_ch1.091: …It's strange. I thought it would feel worse.
hanbi_ch1.093: …I like things when they're almost done. You noticed.
hanbi_ch1.094: When something's finished, people say "that's nice," and put it away. It goes in a box. It goes on a shelf.
hanbi_ch1.095: If it's nearly done, it has to stay out. People have to keep coming back to it.
hanbi_ch1.096: He touches the old note on the lid. *DO NOT PUT AWAY.*
hanbi_ch1.097: …I think I've been this note. About a lot of things.
hanbi_ch1.098: The portrait. I told you I wasn't ready to decide. That's true.
hanbi_ch1.099: But I was also scared. That if I finished your face, tonight would be finished. And you'd go back in the box.
hanbi_ch1.100: He says it plainly, to the puzzle, and then makes himself look up and say the last part to you.
hanbi_ch1.101: …I was afraid of that. I'd rather you knew.
hanbi_ch1.102: "Then we leave it out. Finished, and out. Both."
hanbi_ch1.104: I've packed a lot of boxes. I know what I put in them, and it was never the things I'd finished. It was the things I'd given up on.
hanbi_ch1.106: "I'm much too awkward a shape for a box."
hanbi_ch1.107: …You are. I've been trying to draw it all night.
hanbi_ch1.109: Turn the lid over and hold the marker out to him.
hanbi_ch1.110: There's a marker in the box, dried almost to nothing. You hold it out. He understands at once. He usually does.
hanbi_ch1.111: He takes the pencil from behind his ear and writes on the lid, under the old note, in small careful capitals.
hanbi_ch1.113: …There. Now it's somebody else's problem. In a good way.
hanbi_ch2.001: The lobby is louder than you left it. The noise is coming from the claw machine.
hanbi_ch2.002: It had the bear by the ear. You saw that. Then it let go, and I'd say it was deliberate.
hanbi_ch2.003: It didn't let go. It *released* it. There's a difference, and the bear knows it.
hanbi_ch2.004: Hyunjun is sitting on the floor among the convenience-store bags, sorting what's left into eight fair piles.
hanbi_ch2.005: Hanbi takes his corner of the sofa. The sketchbook comes out. Hyunjun notices at once.
hanbi_ch2.006: Hyung. Draw me. You drew Daniel's face when the building talked. I saw it over your shoulder, and it was good. I'd like one.
hanbi_ch2.007: You drew my face when, exactly?
hanbi_ch2.011: …Any longer and I start being kind. Then it doesn't look like anyone.
hanbi_ch2.012: I'll time it. I'm a fair timekeeper. Go.

hanbi_ch2.015: Hyunjun: a great deal of hair, an easy grin, and a triangle kimbap in one hand, half unwrapped.
hanbi_ch2.016: That's me. No argument. How did the kimbap get in? I wasn't holding one.
hanbi_ch2.018: Daniel gets a level, stubborn brow and, in the corner, a tiny claw with a bear held firmly by one ear.

hanbi_ch2.022: All right. New round. {{playerName}} draws hyung.
hanbi_ch2.024: Seconded. Thirty seconds, same rule. It's only fair.
hanbi_ch2.025: Hanbi goes still. He isn't reluctant. It's more that nobody has ever pointed that question at him before.
hanbi_ch2.026: Then he turns the sketchbook round on his knee and holds out the pencil, the one from behind his ear.
hanbi_ch2.027: …You don't have to be good. I told you. I'd just like to see it.
hanbi_ch2.029: Start with the pencil behind the ear. Get the important things down first.
hanbi_ch2.030: You draw the pencil. It comes out well. It's a very good pencil. After that there are twenty-four seconds left and an entire person to fit round it.
hanbi_ch2.031: Start with the eyes. The way they look at a page.
hanbi_ch2.032: You look up to check. He's looking straight back, holding still the way he asked you to hold still. It costs you four seconds you don't have.
hanbi_ch2.033: Start with the hair. Ask for the blue pencil.
hanbi_ch2.034: He passes the tin without a word. You scribble a sea on top of where a head will shortly need to be. It's bold. You can't undo it now.
hanbi_ch2.035: Thirty seconds turns out to be no time at all. You draw faster. It gets worse. You add a cardigan, because a cardigan is mostly rectangles.
hanbi_ch2.036: Time. Pencils down. Show the court.
hanbi_ch2.038: Nobody says anything for a moment.
hanbi_ch2.039: It's a potato. There's no way round it. A gentle, slightly lopsided potato in a cardigan, with a pencil behind where an ear would go.
hanbi_ch2.040: It's smiling, though. You got that part. It has exactly his small closed smile.
hanbi_ch2.041: I like him. He looks like someone you'd trust with your keys.
hanbi_ch2.042: That's him. I mean it. That's what he's like to be around. Frame it.
hanbi_ch2.043: You risk a look at the subject.
hanbi_ch2.044: Hanbi is laughing the way he does. No sound at all, shoulders going, one hand flat over his eyes.
hanbi_ch2.045: When the hand comes down, he isn't laughing any more. He's looking at the potato quite seriously.
hanbi_ch2.049: Nobody's drawn me before. I'm always the one holding the pencil.
hanbi_ch2.050: "Then it's yours. I'll do a better one when I've had more than thirty seconds."
hanbi_ch2.051: …Don't make it better. Make another one. They're different things.
hanbi_ch2.052: Sign it. Large. With a flourish.
hanbi_ch2.053: You sign it across the bottom corner like a bank manager. He watches every stroke of your name.
hanbi_ch2.055: Turn the book back round to him, and leave your hand on the page a second longer.
hanbi_ch2.056: He takes the book back carefully, his fingers beside yours on the paper, as if the potato might smudge.
hanbi_ch2.057: Trade you, hyung. For the portrait.
hanbi_ch2.058: Hyunjun sets a banana milk on the armrest. Then he sets a second one next to it, for you, as if that went without saying.
hanbi_ch2.059: I'm going back in. The bear and I have unfinished business.
hanbi_ch2.060: I'll spot you one more coin. After that you're negotiating with the machine on your own.
hanbi_ch2.061: They go. The claw machine starts its awful little song again. Hanbi hasn't turned the page.
hanbi_ch2.062: He's gone back to the lobby drawing from the start of the night. The front desk. The Archive Wall, box by box. The sofas.
hanbi_ch2.063: You look at it properly, for the first time since he finished it.
hanbi_ch2.064: Everyone's in it. Songha with his phone up. Charlie mid-question. Justin stealing something out of Hyunjun's bag. Hamin counting heads.
hanbi_ch2.065: And on the end of the far sofa, a row of water bottles on an armrest, and nobody beside them.
hanbi_ch2.069: He looks at the page. It takes him a second to understand the question, and that second tells you more than the answer does.
hanbi_ch2.071: You were also the one sitting there.
hanbi_ch2.072: …I don't usually. Put myself in. It's— the page is for who I'm looking at.
hanbi_ch2.073: He tries to say it like a rule of the craft. It comes out sounding like something smaller and older.
hanbi_ch2.074: …I think I forget. That I'm in the room.
hanbi_ch2.075: "Somebody was sitting there. I saw him. He gave me his water."
hanbi_ch2.077: You remember where I was sitting.
hanbi_ch2.078: Far end. So you could see everyone. It was the first thing I noticed about you.
hanbi_ch2.079: He puts the pencil to the empty cushion. It takes him thirty seconds. He doesn't make it kind.
hanbi_ch2.080: A tall shape, a bit rounded at the shoulders, with a sketchbook on its knee. It's the first drawing of himself you've seen.
hanbi_ch2.081: "May I?" Take the pencil, and put the potato in the empty seat.
hanbi_ch2.082: You draw it small, in the corner of the sofa. A potato in a cardigan, a pencil behind its ear, presiding over seven bottles of water.
hanbi_ch2.083: …That's going to be in there forever.
hanbi_ch2.084: Good. He was there. He should be on the record.
hanbi_ch2.086: Hold out your hand for the pencil. Let him choose who holds it.
hanbi_ch2.087: He looks at your open hand. Then he keeps the pencil, and nods, and bends over the page himself.
hanbi_ch2.088: Nine quick lines. A tall shape with a sketchbook on its knee. He leaves the face for last, from habit. Then he does the face.
hanbi_ch2.089: The lobby drawing has nine people in it now.
hanbi_ch2.090: He holds the book out at arm's length and looks at it the way you look at a photograph that you turn out to be in.
hanbi_ch2.093: …You keep doing that to my things tonight.
hanbi_ch2.094: He opens the banana milk Hyunjun left, and hands you yours with the straw already in. Then he drinks his own. All of it, not the polite half.
hanbi_ch2.095: …Thirty seconds is a long time. When you're the one being looked at.
hanbi_ch2.096: You've been doing it to me all night.
hanbi_ch2.098: A pause. You watch him go back for the sentence.
hanbi_ch2.099: …No. I'm not sorry. I'd do it again. I'm sorry I didn't ask first.
hanbi_ch2.104: Across the lobby the claw machine plays its losing tune. Daniel's voice says, with great dignity, "One more."
hanbi_ch3.001: At a quarter to four, Hanbi checks his phone, puts the sketchbook in his coat, and stands up.
hanbi_ch3.002: …I need to do something. Ten minutes. You can stay here.
hanbi_ch3.004: He hesitates. It's the look of someone who's been asked what's in his bag, when it's only socks.
hanbi_ch3.007: …When we stay somewhere late. I go round. Who's at four percent. Who hasn't had water. Who's fallen asleep somewhere with a draught.
hanbi_ch3.008: It isn't a big thing. It's just— things go better if somebody's checked.
hanbi_ch3.009: Does anyone know you do it?
hanbi_ch3.011: "Can I come? I'd like to see how it's done."
hanbi_ch3.012: …There isn't much to see. That's the point of it.
hanbi_ch3.014: "Does it come with a uniform? A lanyard?"
hanbi_ch3.016: Stand up, and hold out your arms for whatever needs carrying.
hanbi_ch3.017: He looks at your arms for a moment longer than the question needs. Then he nods.
hanbi_ch3.018: From behind the sofa he takes three bottles of water, the phone charger, a packet of tissues and a folded hoodie that isn't his.
hanbi_ch3.019: He looks at the pile. He looks at you. Then, slowly, as if the floor might object, he holds out the water and the tissues.
hanbi_ch3.021: Half is a lot. For you.
hanbi_ch3.023: The corridor of doors is dim and blue. Halfway down it, someone is walking in a slow circle, patting each of his own pockets in turn.
hanbi_ch3.024: …You call it. Before I do. What does he need?
hanbi_ch3.025: "His phone. He's done the same four pockets twice."
hanbi_ch3.027: …You're quick. It took me a month to learn the pockets.
hanbi_ch3.029: …Also true. But look at his hands.
hanbi_ch3.030: Four pockets, patted in order. Then again. Oh.
hanbi_ch3.031: Watch Hanbi watching him, and learn how it's done.
hanbi_ch3.032: He doesn't look at Charlie's face. He looks at his hands, his shoulders, where his feet are pointing. He reads him like a page.
hanbi_ch3.034: Hanbi takes a phone out of his own cardigan. It's fully charged. There's a sticker of a plane on the case.
hanbi_ch3.035: Hyung. That's mine. …Did I hand it to you, or did you rescue it?
hanbi_ch3.036: …You put it on the charger at one. Then you went to look at the rooftop.
hanbi_ch3.037: I did do that. And it's at a hundred. I don't think I've ever got it past sixty. Thank you.
hanbi_ch3.038: Charlie pockets the phone. Then he notices you, and the water in your arms, and puts it together.
hanbi_ch3.039: You're helping. Good. He should have help. He's just never asked for it.
hanbi_ch3.040: He says it lightly, as a plain fact, and goes off down the hall with one hand raised over his shoulder.
hanbi_ch3.043: …He's almost never wrong. He just arrives late.
hanbi_ch3.044: The practice room is lit by one strip light. Somebody's phone is propped on the floor against the mirror, playing a beat at half volume.
hanbi_ch3.045: Justin is dancing. Not rehearsing. Just moving, the way other people pace. He spots you in the mirror, finishes the eight-count anyway, and lands it.
hanbi_ch3.047: There's already a bottle in his hand. You didn't see Hanbi cross the room, and you were standing next to him.
hanbi_ch3.048: See, that's the thing about him. You never catch it happening. I turn round and there's water. It's like living with a very thoughtful ghost.
hanbi_ch3.049: And tonight the ghost has an apprentice.
hanbi_ch3.051: Respect. Start at the bottom. Work up to chargers.
hanbi_ch3.052: Hanbi opens the window a hand's width, because the mirror has started to fog. He hangs the folded hoodie on the barre. It's Justin's, of course.
hanbi_ch3.054: He says it to the hoodie, more or less. Then he looks at you, and for half a second he's entirely serious.
hanbi_ch3.055: Hey. Make him drink one too. He counts us and forgets there's one more.
hanbi_ch3.057: Fast learner. Okay. I've got sixteen more bars in me. Go and haunt someone else.
hanbi_ch3.058: Back round to the front desk. One bottle of water left. It's in your hands, and you've been thinking about Justin's instruction the whole way down the corridor.
hanbi_ch3.059: Songha is behind the desk with a clipboard. You don't know where he found a clipboard. It seems likely it found him.
hanbi_ch3.060: Oh, good. You're both here. I've got an item.
hanbi_ch3.062: Nothing. *I've* got an item. For you. 03:55: Hanbi sits down. You've skipped it four times tonight, so I've moved it four times.
hanbi_ch3.064: Hyung. You've always been on the schedule.
hanbi_ch3.065: He turns the clipboard round. It's a page in his tidy handwriting, soft at the corners from being carried about. It's clearly older than tonight.

hanbi_ch3.067: Hanbi reads it. Then he reads it again, more slowly. He looks like a man counting his change and finding there's too much.
hanbi_ch3.069: The rota. For you. It's been running about a year.
hanbi_ch3.071: Did you think the kimbap walked? You do the rounds. We know. Everybody knows. We leave you to it because it's how you say things.
hanbi_ch3.072: We just thought someone ought to say it back.

hanbi_ch3.077: Hanbi looks at the page for a long moment. He isn't embarrassed. He's taking it in slowly, the way he takes in a face before he draws it.
hanbi_ch3.078: …The refills. I thought I was just— not drinking much.
hanbi_ch3.079: Justin's very quiet about it. {{playerName}}, he'll be pleased it went a whole year unnoticed.
hanbi_ch3.080: Hold the last bottle out to him. "This one's yours. Drink it where I can see."

hanbi_ch3.083: I know. You have been since the lobby.
hanbi_ch3.084: …You call it before I do, now.

hanbi_ch3.086: Absolutely not. It's laminated. It's classified. …I'm adding you to it.

hanbi_ch3.089: Put the bottle in his hand. Pull out the chair behind the desk. Say nothing.

hanbi_ch3.099: …Like finding out I've been in the drawing the whole time.

hanbi_ch4.001: The rain has thinned to nothing. The rooftop is wet and wide and smells of cold concrete. Below, the city is a loose handful of lights.
hanbi_ch4.002: Hanbi goes straight to the low wall on the alley side and looks over, the way you'd check on something left in the oven.
hanbi_ch4.004: The alley behind the laundromat, from above. The vending machine, small as a matchbox, with its one red button. The laundromat sign, still on.
hanbi_ch4.005: And the STUDIO 25 sign with its crooked 2. You're looking at it from the back, and the letters are the wrong way round.
hanbi_ch4.006: …I've drawn this building from every side except this one. Tomorrow there'll be scaffolding. I wanted the last side.

hanbi_ch4.008: Pin the page flat with both hands. "I've got it. Draw."
hanbi_ch4.009: Your hands are on either side of the paper, and his pencil moves between them. He's careful at the edges.
hanbi_ch4.010: Put the hundred-won coin from under the sofa on one corner. "Paperweight. It owes us."
hanbi_ch4.011: …Six years under a sofa. Now it's got a job.
hanbi_ch4.012: The coin holds one corner and you hold the other three. It's doing about a quarter of the work and would get all of the credit.
hanbi_ch4.013: Stand on the windward side of him, so the page lies still.
hanbi_ch4.014: You don't say why you've moved. After a moment the page settles, and he glances at you, and his shoulder comes to rest a little nearer yours.
hanbi_ch4.015: He draws the alley in long downward lines. He's quick with the walls and slow with the lights.
hanbi_ch4.016: You hold the page. Far below, a taxi goes by. Neither of you says anything for a while, and it's comfortable.
hanbi_ch4.017: Can I ask you something that isn't about tonight?
hanbi_ch4.019: What happens after? For you. For all of you.
hanbi_ch4.020: The pencil doesn't stop, but it slows.
hanbi_ch4.021: …We practise. We wait. We practise more. One day someone tells us a date.
hanbi_ch4.022: …That's what I say when the others ask.
hanbi_ch4.024: …I'm the eldest. At two in the morning someone always asks if it's going to be okay. I say yes.
hanbi_ch4.026: …I don't know. I say yes because it's needed. It isn't a lie. It's— water. You hand it over.

hanbi_ch4.028: …Do you know what I've never said?

hanbi_ending_beside.049: …In case I lose it. It should know where to go.
hanbi_ending_beside.050: …And in case you lose track. Of where to go. It's written down now. Writing stays.
hanbi_ending_beside.051: You've had four addresses, and none of them ever had you on somebody else's cover. You read the line twice, like a word you're learning to spell.
hanbi_ending_beside.052: You take the sharpener out of your coat pocket. *Put it somewhere you're staying. It needs to be clamped to something.*
hanbi_ending_beside.053: The sofa has a wooden rail along the back. You fit the clamp over it and tighten the screw with a hundred-won coin.
hanbi_ending_beside.055: It goes where the sofa goes. The sofa goes where you all go. I've decided I'm easy to find.
hanbi_ending_beside.056: He looks at the sharpener for a long moment. It's a grey machine bolted to a terrible sofa in the morning sun. He is plainly, quietly happy, and he doesn't hide it.
hanbi_ending_beside.057: …Then I'll always have a sharp pencil. And you'll always have to come and use it.

hanbi_ending_beside.061: The sofa is staying exactly where it is. The van's at nine. Hanbi, I need a charger. I'm at two percent, and I've got a van to manage.
hanbi_ending_beside.062: Hanbi reaches for his cardigan pocket, and stops. You're already holding it out to Songha. It's still wound in his neat figure of eight.
hanbi_ending_beside.063: …Ah. There are two of you now.
hanbi_ending_beside.065: He hands you a bottle of water from somewhere. You drink half and hand it back, and he drinks the rest without being asked.
hanbi_ending_beside.066: *I hope, by the time you read this, you've found a place you want to stay.*
hanbi_ending_beside.067: You have. It's orange, it's on a pavement, and it leaves in a van at nine. You know exactly where it's going.
hanbi_ending_beside.068: You stay on it, next to him, until then.
hanbi_ending_someday.003: …It's how I do everything. I didn't know anyone else wanted it that way.
hanbi_ending_someday.004: RECORD 01 — OWNER: HANBI. SELECTED FOR PRESERVATION.
hanbi_ending_someday.005: Status: in progress. I invented that status tonight. I am pleased to be using it again so soon.
hanbi_ending_someday.006: Light runs out of the wall and into the small rectangle of glass on the desk. The lounge, the rain, the orange sofa. A figure at a desk, and on its face a single soft line.
hanbi_ending_someday.007: There's a line on the face now. There wasn't one before. I'd call that progress.
hanbi_ending_someday.008: I like it like that. It's like a film that stops just before the last scene. You walk home still inside it.
hanbi_ending_someday.010: For now. That's the good part.
hanbi_ending_someday.011: Hanbi picks up the glass card and holds it out to you in both hands.
hanbi_ending_someday.012: …Keep it for me. I'd like to visit it.
hanbi_ending_someday.013: "Visit." He's making appointments. I'll leave room in the calendar.
hanbi_ending_someday.014: There's a bench outside the laundromat, under the sign that's always on. Behind the glass one dryer is still turning. It's somebody's forgotten towels, going round and round.
hanbi_ending_someday.015: You sit. He sits. The alley is peach and grey and very quiet. The STUDIO 25 sign is across the way, with its crooked 2, the right way round again.
hanbi_ending_someday.016: He has his hands round the folded *FUTURE LETTER* card. He turns it over once, and puts it down on the bench between you.
hanbi_ending_someday.017: …I said it in the drawn room. I'd like to say it again. Out here, where the rain's real.
hanbi_ending_someday.019: …In the drawn room I said I wanted to see you again. I didn't know what it was yet. I've found the rest of the sentence since.
hanbi_ending_someday.021: There's no dash. He looks at you the whole way through it.
hanbi_ending_someday.023: It's out, in ordinary daylight, on a bench. The dryer goes on turning. Nothing breaks. It's the easiest true thing you've said in years.
hanbi_ending_someday.025: …I'd thought about what to say if you said it back. It turns out I'd rather just look at you for a minute.
hanbi_ending_someday.026: "I don't want it to be something that happened because a building was closing."

hanbi_ending_someday.028: "We've been awake for twenty-two hours. I'd like to like you on some sleep."
hanbi_ending_someday.029: …I'd like that too. I think I'd be better at it.
hanbi_ending_someday.030: …An ordinary day, then. One we chose.
hanbi_ending_someday.031: "I've started a lot of things the week before I left. I want this one to start on a day I'm staying."
hanbi_ending_someday.032: …Then we pick a day. One where nobody's leaving. I'd like that more than I can— no. I'd like that very much.
hanbi_ending_someday.033: He takes the new pencil from behind his ear. He tears the card along its fold, slowly, so that there isn't a ragged edge. *FUTURE* on one half, *LETTER* on the other.
hanbi_ending_someday.034: …It was raining. The first time. It was twenty to four in the afternoon.
hanbi_ending_someday.035: …The first rain of spring. 15:40. This bench.

hanbi_ending_someday.043: And until then? Spring's a long way off.
hanbi_ending_someday.044: He looks almost offended, very gently, in the way he is when someone supposes he's only brought one charger.
hanbi_ending_someday.045: …Until then I need sittings. Every week. I'm slow. You've seen how slow.

hanbi_ending_someday.048: I already know they're not about the drawing.
hanbi_ending_someday.049: …I know you know. I want to say it on the day anyway. Out loud. With the right weather.
hanbi_ending_someday.050: He unfolds the old portrait on his knee. There's the oval, and the one soft line where a mouth might go.
hanbi_ending_someday.051: He adds a second line. It's short, near one eye. It's the beginning of the look you get when you're about to laugh.

hanbi_ending_someday.053: "I'll be there. I'm writing it down too."

hanbi_ending_someday.060: Put the half-card in your inside pocket, with the things you don't pack in boxes.
hanbi_ending_someday.061: It lies flat against your ribs. *FUTURE.* For the first time in a long while, the word has a date on it.

hanbi_ending_someday.063: The sun clears the roof of the laundromat. The sign overhead is still on. It doesn't know it's morning.
hanbi_ending_someday.064: The sharpener is heavy in your coat. You have an appointment in a city in spring. You've left every city you've lived in, and it has always been in spring.
hanbi_ending_someday.065: You won't be leaving this one. You've got it in writing.
hanbi_ending_someday.066: Hanbi. Has anyone seen Hanbi? I need a charger.
hanbi_ending_someday.067: The voice comes down the alley. Hanbi stands up and holds out his hand. He isn't leading you. It's there if you want it.
